h: Tropics in the Morning, the Rest of Leeds by Afternoon
p: Tropical World has been delighting Leeds families for decades, and it's a real local institution. Many grown-ups who visited as kids now bring their own children, and it's easy to see why it's lasted. It's affordable, friendly and the right size for little ones who aren't up to a huge zoo trek.

It's warm and humid inside, so dress in layers, and be ready to carry a few coats on the way round. The paths wind through the different zones, so take your time and keep your eyes open, because some of the smaller animals are easy to miss among the plants. School holidays and rainy weekends are naturally the busiest times, so arriving early can mean a calmer wander, and the café is a handy pit stop before or after your visit.

Getting here is easy too. Roundhay Park has several car parks, and buses run regularly from Leeds city centre to the park, so you don't have to drive. Combine Tropical World with a walk round Waterloo Lake, past the Castle folly perched on the hillside, and you have a brilliant free half-day.

If you've got the rest of the day free, Leeds has loads of other places to visit. The Royal Armouries at Leeds Dock houses the national collection of arms and armour, and it's free to get in. Kirkstall Abbey, the ruins of a Cistercian monastery just west of the city centre, is beautiful to wander around. Leeds City Museum in the centre covers everything from natural history to ancient worlds, while the Thackray Museum of Medicine tells the gruesome and fascinating story of medicine through the ages. There's no shortage of ways to fill a weekend in Leeds.
